data.title: Global Survey Uncovers an "Aloneware" Crisis: Isolated AI Development Threatens Enterprise Stability and Adds Maintenance Costs
data.description:
Global Survey Uncovers an "Aloneware" Crisis: Isolated AI Development Threatens Enterprise Stability and Adds Maintenance Costs

Global Survey Uncovers an "Aloneware" Crisis: Isolated AI Development Threatens Enterprise Stability and Adds Maintenance Costs

PR Newswire

MCLEAN, Va., Nov. 20, 2026

Two-thirds of AI decision-makers and IT leaders say standalone coding assistants lead to "aloneware": software that's difficult to support, understand, and maintain.

MCLEAN, Va., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Appian (Nasdaq: APPN), an AI automation leader, today released new research asking AI decision-makers and IT leaders about AI-assisted development. They found that enterprise investments in fast-tracked AI software development are creating an unexpected drain on corporate innovation capital, with 82% of enterprise leaders allocating at least 10% of their current technology innovation funds to test, deploy, maintain, update, integrate, and/or repair isolated AI software builds.

Enterprise investments in AI software development are creating an unexpected drain on corporate innovation capital.

In the global survey of 851 respondents at large enterprises, Appian defines a new term: "aloneware." These are applications built or modified with AI-assisted development tools outside an approved enterprise platform environment. While these tools accelerate initial code creation, organizations face mounting friction to understand AI-generated applications and keep them functional, secure, and integrated over time.

Upfront speed creates downstream work

Initial build speed is failing to deliver long-term efficiency. Just over seven in 10 (71%1) enterprise leaders surveyed report that while standalone AI tools accelerate development, they are spending more time across testing, system integration, troubleshooting, scaling, and/or deployment.

According to Matt Calkins, CEO of Appian, "Some people get so excited about 'free' software that they forget the risks. Enterprises can now create tech debt faster than ever before."

Aloneware diverts strategic innovation budgets

The operational burden of maintaining software built outside a platform is directly diverting capital away from strategic growth. More than eight in 10 (82%) enterprise leaders surveyed report allocating at least 10% of their current technology innovation budgets to testing, deploying, maintaining, updating, integrating, and/or repairing software built outside a platform environment. And 43% of those surveyed currently allocate at least 20% of the budget—a figure that 64% expect to allocate within the next two years, indicating that the financial drain is accelerating quickly.

Compounding these budget demands, more than two-thirds (68%2) of enterprise leaders report unexpected post-launch costs or resources tied directly to security, governance, and compliance remediation.

The support void and the need for platforms

When isolated AI applications break, organizations face a critical support void. More than two-thirds (68%3) of leaders find it challenging to access accountable technical support when problems arise with applications built outside a platform, while 66%3 report difficulties keeping code, architecture, dependencies, and system integrations up to date.

Against this backdrop, 73%4 of respondents state that a shared architectural foundation would improve their ability to control total cost of ownership and 71%4 say it would help them maintain software over time.

"The most important applications in enterprises need support," Calkins adds. "If you vibe-code them, there will be nobody to turn to when problems occur. Using AI to build applications on a commercial platform combines the speed of AI with the reliability of supported technology."

To access the complete research findings and executive report, visit appian.com/aloneware.

About the research

The research was conducted by Censuswide among 851 senior decision-makers who primarily work in AI/Engineering or IT, work at large enterprises (5,000 employees or more, or annual revenue exceeding $1 billion), and who work on at least three software systems annually. Respondents were based in Australia, the USA, New Zealand, France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK. Data was collected between 21 and 30 October 2026.

Censuswide is a member of the Market Research Society (MRS) and the British Polling Council (BPC), and a signatory of the Global Data Quality Pledge. The research adheres to the MRS Code of Conduct and ESOMAR principles.

  1. 'Completely agree' and 'Mostly agree' responses combined
  2. 'Significant additional cost or resource' and 'Some additional cost or resource' responses combined
  3. 'Very challenging' and 'Somewhat challenging' responses combined
  4. 'Improve significantly' and 'Improve somewhat' responses combined

About Appian

Appian provides AI automation for the most important business processes at the world's largest organizations.  

On the Appian Platform, customers build AI-powered processes that accelerate work, reduce cost, and manage risk. Our platform is known for its unique power, reliability, and scale. We've been automating processes for more than 25 years and have proven expertise in enterprise operations. For more information, visit appian.com. [Nasdaq: APPN]

Follow Appian: LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and X.

data.title: Consumer Sentiment Climbed in November
data.description:
By Matt Grossman

Consumer sentiment improved in November, according to the University of Michigan's monthly survey, yet it remains near historically low levels that reflect Americans' widespread economic frustrations.

The survey's sentiment index ended November at 51.5, a rise from 48 in October. That also was an improvement from the preliminary November reading of 51 published earlier this month.

Stock-market volatility dented the mood among wealthier Americans who own more assets, said Joanne Hsu, the survey's director. By contract, sentiment improved among low- and middle-wealth consumers.

Democrats and independents reported brighter economic expectations after this month's blue-wave midterm elections rebuked Republicans' economic stewardship. Republicans reported a decline in economic expectations.

data.title: Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. Announces Third Quarter Financial Results
data.description:
Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. Announces Third Quarter Financial Results

Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQX: MNMB), the parent company of TownBridge Bank, reported net income available to common shareholders through the third quarter of 2026 of $12.84 million, or $9.13 per share, compared with earnings of $2.30 million, or $1.73 per share, in the same period of the prior year. Gross income through the third quarter totaled $73.34 million, an increase of 82.02% from the prior year. Balance sheet footings increased by 36.95% to $1.30 billion during the 12 months ended September 30, 2026. Net loans grew to $692.90 million over the trailing 12 months from $466.73 million, an increase of 48.46%. Total deposits increased 58.65% during the same period, from $603.81 million at September 30, 2025, to $957.97 million. Significant growth in the balance sheet and in earnings is primarily the result of the successful acquisition of Farmers-Merchants Bank, Breaux Bridge, LA (FM Bank), which closed on April 1, 2026.

Selected financial highlights:

  • Net loans increased to $692.90 million at the end of the third quarter, up from $677.13 million at the end of the second quarter.
  • Total interest income during the third quarter increased to $16.99 million from $12.67 million during the same period in 2025, an increase of 34.11%. Net interest income for the quarter totaled $13.24 million, compared with $9.69 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Deposit costs totaled 74 basis points in the third quarter of 2026, essentially unchanged from 73 basis points in the second quarter of 2026.
  • The ratio of loans past due 30-89 days stood at 2.54% of total loans at the end of the third quarter of 2026, an increase from 1.70% at the end of the second quarter. The ratio of non-accrual loans totaled 1.87% of total loans at the end of the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1.94% at the end of the second quarter. The Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) totaled $7.95 million, or 1.13% of total loans.
  • Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI) mark-to-market losses in the securities portfolio totaled ($11.80 million) at the end of the third quarter of 2026, representing 3.05% of the $386.69 million securities portfolio. The increase in AOCI from ($5.81 million) during the second quarter is a result of increases in market rates during the quarter.
  • On-balance sheet liquidity levels remain healthy, with cash and cash equivalents totaling $94.42 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026. In addition to these large cash balances, the Company's investment portfolio remains highly liquid, with a significant portion of the portfolio able to be liquidated with minimal losses.
  • In addition to the sizable on-balance sheet liquidity position, the Company has more than $200 million in additional borrowing capacity at the Federal Home Loan Bank of Dallas and the Federal Reserve.

“We continued a strong earnings trend in the third quarter of 2026, with pre-tax, pre-provision earnings of approximately $2.26 million. This was inclusive of a $158 thousand loss on securities sales as we repositioned the portfolio to better fit the bank after our acquisition of Farmers-Merchants Bank earlier this year,” remarked Casey Hill, the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He continued: “Core earnings continue to accelerate as we realize certain efficiencies after our most recent merger. We do expect these efficiencies to further materialize as we undergo our core and systems conversion in January of 2027. Since the acquisition of FM Bank, we have been operating two core systems along with several other duplicative systems that, once fully merged, are expected to produce significant cost savings.”

“In addition,” continued Hill, “our teams across our Family of Brands continue to perform well. The increase in revenue from our legacy brands, paired with the continued high performance of the FM Bank team bodes well for continued lift in future earnings. While we are experiencing tailwinds in the form of slight elevations in past due loans, we feel confident that the bulk of these should be resolved prior to year-end and are not indicative of broader erosion in our loan portfolio. We are very optimistic about financial performance going forward.”

“Our third quarter results reflect the strong progress our teams are making in bringing FM Bank into our Family of Brands operating model,” remarked Clayton Legear, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer. “Our talented bankers have done an outstanding job of integrating a sizable new brand while continuing to operate our legacy brands at ever stronger levels. We remain encouraged that our operating model allows our brand bankers to serve their clients and communities with the same care and attention they always have and to drive strong results. We are on track for our core systems conversion in January 2027, and we are excited about the enhanced efficiencies and capabilities that will follow.”

Legear continued: “The third quarter also marked an important milestone for our Company. Effective September 28, 2026, our bank charter name officially changed from Merchants & Marine Bank to TownBridge Bank, providing a shared corporate identity for our growing Family of Brands. While our bank charter name has changed, our commitment to our Family of Brands operating model has not. Each of our brands will continue to retain their unique identity, and to be led by local bankers who know their clients, understand their communities, and make decisions close to home. Backed by our Battle-Ready Balance Sheet, our talented team of bankers in every Brand, and the strong momentum building across our Family of Brands, we are better positioned than ever for the future.”

Share Repurchase Program

The share repurchase program authorized by the Board of Directors in the second quarter, covering up to three percent (3%) of the Company's outstanding common stock, remains in effect through June 30, 2027.

Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQX: MNMB) is the parent company of TownBridge Bank, a Mississippi chartered community bank serving the Gulf South region. Originally founded in 1899 as Merchants & Marine Bank and reborn during 1932, the Bank adopted the TownBridge Bank name in 2026 to provide a shared charter identity for its growing Family of Brands while allowing its community banking and financial services brands to retain the local identifies, leadership, and relationships that make them distinctive. The Bank offers banking services to customers in Southern Mississippi and Coastal Alabama under its legacy Merchants & Marine Bank brand, in Southeastern Louisiana through its Mississippi River Bank brand, and in the Acadiana Region of Louisiana through its Farmers-Merchants Bank brand. It offers mortgage financing through its Canvas Mortgage brand, cannabis banking through its CannaFirst Financial brand, and access to government-guaranteed credit through its Voyager Lending brand. It provides bank operational, risk, and support services through its Community of Resources bank services brand. For more information on Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc., visit https://townbridge.bank/investors/

data.title: This closely watched investing guru just sold all of his stocks
data.description:
By Brett Arends

A widely-followed market commentator says he's selling all of his stocks.

Panmure Liberum strategist and widely-followed stock market commentator Joachim Klement has effectively had his personal retirement portfolio 100% invested in stocks for many years.

Thursday morning he sold everything.

"The S&P 500 has now broken below its 200-day moving average, and hence, at the end of European trading, I will sell my personal holdings in stocks and move into long-term government bonds," he has written to clients in his morning note.

"While this indicator is not foolproof, market dynamics have turned decisively bearish, in our view," he adds. "We have consistently warned of an AI bubble since May and have become more bearish since September." Klement shocked Wall Street early last month when he warned that the collapsing AI bubble would drag down the entire market with it, and predicted the S&P 500 would end next year at just 5,000, a third below the current level.

The 200-day moving average signal is a stock-market timing mechanism with a long pedigree. It has been popularized among modern investors by Cambria Investments' Meb Faber, who has pointed out that it has helped investors escape the worst bear markets of the past 100 years.

Selling out of the market when it fell below the 200-day average, and buying back in when it goes back above the average, has dramatically reduced long-term portfolio volatility in the past, Faber found. Someone who simply bought and held didn't necessarily earn less over the long haul, he found. But, oh boy, they slept easier.

Following this rule kept an investor out of the worst of the bear market during the dot-com bust and the global financial crisis.

The S&P 500 is now below the 200-day average (orange line).

When I communicated with Klement early last week, as the Jensen Huang affair helped accelerate turmoil in technology stocks, he predicted that the S&P 500 SPX would finally break below the 200-day moving average around the middle of this week. And so it has happened, though as everyone (including Klement) will tell you, it's better to be lucky than to be smart.

There is never a shortage of people predicting doom and gloom, and the late Nobel laureate Paul Samuelson famously said decades ago that the stock market had successfully predicted nine of the last five U.S. recessions. But London-based Klement, a former board member of the US CFA Research Institute, is no gadfly or extremist. He is widely respected on both sides of the Atlantic and is broadly a cautious strategist.

Related: The good news: Bubble predictions vastly outnumber actual episodes. The bad: There may be a 97% chance of one, right now.

(He also earned extra fame recently for successfully predicting the winners of the 2014, 2018 and 2022 soccer World Cups, as part of an experiment to prove the impossibility of predictions, before this year's team, the Dutch, fell short).

His reasons for turning extremely defensive and moving into bonds are worth exploring.

It is no secret among professional economists that the investment assumptions needed to support the Wall Street AI mania are heroic.

This is not the same as claiming AI isn't a transformational technology. It is. But that does not mean the hyperscalers, and their billionaire tech bro CEOs, are going to earn good returns on the trillions of dollars they are pouring into competing data centers.

For reference, over the past 200 or so years other inventions, such as the canals, railways, motor cars, airplanes, radio, and most recently fiber optic cable all ended up transforming the economy and the world. But along the way most of the people who invested in these technologies ended up losing their shirts.

(Those who are convinced that the AI boom is not a financial bubble, and that the hyperscalers will quickly earn excellent returns on the trillions of dollars they are spending, can probably stop reading right now. Only time will tell one way or another.)

Among the recent signs cited by Klement that the AI bubble is deflating: Falling prices for AI tokens, the slowing revenue growth revealed for example, in the Anthropic IPO prospectus, and growing stock market restlessness about AI capex. He also includes the growing signs of circular financing in the AI sector, so redolent of the infamous "vendor financing" of the dotcom mania.

He might have added recent signs of extreme stock-market reactions, all of which suggest investors have become jumpy. AI related stocks that have been in serious turmoil for months include chip giant Intel (INTC), memory giant SanDisk (SNDK), Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM), South Korea's SK Hynix (SKHY), and industry flagship Nvidia (NVDA), whose stock was in freefall well before the Jensen Huang scandal.

Bubbles, ultimately, are about mass psychology and not just economics. They survive on belief. What caused the tech or dot-com bubble to burst in March 2000? Even today, nobody really knows or can agree. Manias have been compared to those Road Runner cartoons, where Wile E. Coyote races off the end of the cliff. He's fine until he looks down.

Klement thinks the market has probably just looked down. He says clients have been asking him for months when he was going to back his bearish views with his own money, and he has repeatedly said he was waiting for the S&P 500 to fall below the 200-day moving average as his trigger.

Selling out of the market when the index falls below the 200-day moving average isn't for everyone. Far from it. Most investors may have very good reasons for ignoring this idea completely. It raises your trading costs, and can trigger capital gains taxes if you are selling stocks or funds in taxable accounts. And it can also involve you in a lot of trading, especially if the market bounces around the 200-day moving average for a long time. You can be selling, buying, selling and buying. Even if you are monitoring your portfolio daily.

Klement says he will buy back in if and when the market goes back above the 200-day average, and that if it goes up and down repeatedly he could be in for a lot of churn. "This way I may incur a lot of portfolio churn, but I know I will be out of stocks when the AI bubble bursts and back in if setbacks are temporary in nature and not persistent."

As for the current call, "I may be wrong, and this is not the bubble bursting, but if that is the case, my trading rule will ensure I go back in without too much opportunity cost," he adds.

This is certainly not a recommendation that readers follow the same strategy. On the other hand, this might be an excellent time to review the amount of risk you are taking in your portfolio, and ask yourself if it's the right amount.

-Brett Arends

data.title: American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA): EL NIÑO AND WINTER WEATHER: HOW TO PROTECT YOUR HOME, CAR AND FINANCES BEFORE THE STORM
data.description:
American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA): EL NIÑO AND WINTER WEATHER: HOW TO PROTECT YOUR HOME, CAR AND FINANCES BEFORE THE STORM

American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA): EL NIÑO AND WINTER WEATHER: HOW TO PROTECT YOUR HOME, CAR AND FINANCES BEFORE THE STORM

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Nov. 20, 2026

WHY CONSUMERS SHOULD TAKE STEPS NOW TO PROTECT HOMES, VEHICLES AND FINANCES BEFORE WINTER STORM RISKS INCREASE

WASHINGTON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

BACKGROUND:
When severe winter weather strikes, the time to prepare has already passed. This year, a potentially significant El Niño weather pattern could bring heavier rainfall, flooding, mudslides and severe storms throughout the winter months. Some forecasters are comparing current conditions to the powerful 1982-83 El Niño, which caused widespread flooding and billions of dollars in damage across California. While the extent of its impact remains uncertain, consumers should review their insurance coverage and take practical steps to reduce risk before winter weather arrives.

Experience the full interactive Multichannel News Release here: https://www.multivu.com/american-property-casualty-insurance-association/9361253-en-apcia-el-nino-winter-weather-tips

Recent years have shown that severe flooding can happen almost anywhere, often with little warning. Consumers should not assume they are protected from flood losses simply because they do not live near the coast. Flooding remains one of the costliest natural disasters, yet many homeowners are uninsured for flood damage.

While no one can predict exactly how El Niño and other weather conditions will unfold, preparing now can help reduce disruption and financial loss. In this interview, you'll learn the steps consumers can take to protect their property and finances. Because many homeowners only discover after a flood that their standard homeowner's policy does not cover flood damage, you'll discover why now is the time to review your coverage and identify potential gaps.

Cardinal Infrastructure Group Inc. (CDNL) Securities Investigation Notice - Levi & Korsinsky

Cardinal Infrastructure Group Inc. (CDNL) Securities Investigation Notice - Levi & Korsinsky

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026

Cardinal Infrastructure Group told shareholders in August to expect $880-$900 million in 2026 revenue and 16% to 18% adjusted EBITDA margins. Its third-quarter margin came in near 4.2%, and the full-year outlook was withdrawn.

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cardinal Infrastructure Group Inc. (Nasdaq: CDNL) shareholders were guided to 16% to 18% adjusted EBITDA margins for 2026. Then the Company reported a third-quarter margin of approximately 4.2%, an approximately $11 million net loss, and the withdrawal of its 2026 guidance. If you bought CDNL on the strength of that outlook and lost money, you may have the right to seek recovery. Shareholders who suffered losses are encouraged to submit their CDNL loss details now or to contact Joseph E. Levi, Esq. via email at jlevi@levikorsinsky.com or by telephone at (212) 363-7500.

On August 11, 2026, Cardinal raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $880-$900 million. The increase lifted the midpoint by $210 million. The Company also set its adjusted EBITDA margin target at 16% to 18%. On the earnings call that day, Chairman and CEO Jeremy Spivey said the Company believed "with conviction that we will hit the 16% to 18% guidance for adjusted EBITDA."

The third-quarter 2026 report showed a gross margin of 5.4% and an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 4.2%, down from 17.5% a year earlier. That is roughly one-quarter of the low end of the guided range. Management cited project-cost revisions, residential pricing pressure, lower initial bid margins, and higher fuel and transportation costs. Cardinal withdrew its full-year revenue and margin guidance and postponed its Hughes Brothers acquisition. Levi & Korsinsky is investigating potential securities law violations connected to the Company's 2026 guidance.

Investors who lost money on Cardinal Infrastructure Group shares can find out whether they may be eligible to recover or call (212) 363-7500.

Levi & Korsinsky, LLP | Top 50 Securities Firm | (212) 363-7500 | www.zlk.com

Frequently Asked Questions About the CDNL Investigation

Q: Which statements are being investigated as potentially misleading?A: The investigation concerns whether Cardinal Infrastructure Group Inc. made materially false or misleading statements regarding its full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance. When the Company disclosed its third-quarter 2026 results, an approximately $11 million net loss, and the withdrawal of its full-year guidance, the stock price declined sharply.

Q: When did Cardinal Infrastructure Group allegedly mislead investors?A: The investigation concerns statements made before Cardinal Infrastructure Group reported its third-quarter 2026 results. These statements allegedly caused investors to purchase securities at inflated prices.

Q: What do CDNL investors need to do right now?A: Investors may gather brokerage records showing purchase dates, share quantities, and prices paid. Submit your information for a no-cost, no-obligation evaluation of your potential recovery. No immediate action is required to remain eligible to participate in the investigation.

Q: What documents do I need to participate?A: Brokerage statements or trade confirmations showing purchase dates, share quantities, prices paid, and any subsequent sale dates and prices.

Q: What if I already sold my CDNL shares -- can I still recover losses?A: Yes. Eligibility is based on when you purchased, not whether you still hold the shares. Investors who bought CDNL and sold at a loss may still participate in the investigation.

Q: What does it cost me to participate?A: There is no upfront cost to submit your information and review whether you may be eligible to recover. If you choose to participate in any resulting action, these matters are generally handled on a contingency basis. Any attorneys' fees and expenses are subject to court approval.

Q: What if I live outside the United States?A: U.S. securities investigations generally cover purchases on U.S. exchanges regardless of the investor's country of residence.

data.title: AM Best Affirms Credit Ratings of Delphi Financial Group, Inc. and Its Subsidiaries; Upgrades Issuer Credit Rating of Standard Security Life Insurance Company of New York
data.description:
AM Best Affirms Credit Ratings of Delphi Financial Group, Inc. and Its Subsidiaries; Upgrades Issuer Credit Rating of Standard Security Life Insurance Company of New York

AM Best has affirmed the Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of A++ (Superior) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Ratings (Long-Term ICRs) of “aa+” (Superior) of the life/health subsidiaries of Delphi Financial Group, Inc. (DFG) (Wilmington, DE): Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company (Schaumburg, IL) and First Reliance Standard Life Insurance Company (New York, NY) (together referred to as Reliance Standard). AM Best also has affirmed the FSR of A++ (Superior) and the Long-Term ICRs of “aa+” (Superior) of DFG’s property/casualty subsidiaries: Safety National Casualty Corporation, Safety Specialty Insurance Company and Safety First Insurance Company (all domiciled in St. Louis, MO) (together referred to as Safety National). DFG is a direct subsidiary of Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance Co., Ltd., whose ultimate parent is Tokio Marine Holdings, Inc. (Tokio Marine), Japan’s largest non-life insurance organization.

Concurrently, AM Best has affirmed the Long Term ICR of “a+” (Excellent) and the Long-Term Issue Credit Rating (Long-Term IR) of “a-” (Excellent) of DFG. In addition, AM Best has affirmed the Long-Term IRs of “aa+” (Superior) on the outstanding medium-term notes issued under the funding agreement backed-securities program of Reliance Standard Life Global Funding II. The outlook of these Credit Ratings (ratings) is stable.

Lastly, AM Best has upgraded the Long-Term ICR to “a+” (Excellent) from “a” (Excellent) and affirmed the FSR of A (Excellent) of Standard Security Life Insurance Company of New York (SSL) (New York, NY). The outlook of the Long-Term ICR has been revised to stable from positive, while the outlook of the FSR is stable. (Please see below for a detailed list of the Long-Term IRs.)

The ratings of Reliance Standard reflect its balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its strong operating performance, neutral business profile and very strong enterprise risk management (ERM). Reliance Standard’s ratings also reflect the strategic importance and high degree of integration with Tokio Marine. In addition, the group maintains the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), and it has produced historical levels of operating earnings in recent periods. The ratings also consider Reliance Standard’s reasonable operating leverage, financial leverage, and interest coverage at the intermediate holding company, DFG, as well as the group’s very strong risk management capabilities.

Partially offsetting these positive rating factors is the group’s investment profile, which includes elevated levels of higher risk and less liquid assets. Commercial mortgage loans and below-investment-grade bonds both exceed industry averages and AM Best will continue to monitor these allocations.

The ratings of Safety National reflect its balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as strongest, as well as its strong operating performance, neutral business profile and very strong ERM. Safety National’s ratings also consider the group’s strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by BCAR, historically profitable overall operating performance and return measures that far outpace the industry, as well as its position as an industry leader in excess workers’ compensation.

Partially offsetting these positive rating factors is Safety National’s exposure to schedule BA assets. This allocation represents sizable portions of Safety National’s invested assets and surplus and is elevated compared with its peer composite.

The ratings of SSL reflect its balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as strongest, as well as its adequate operating performance, limited business profile and very strong ERM. SSL’s ratings also reflect its high degree of integration and strategic importance to Tokio Marine. The company maintains the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by BCAR, with a conservative portfolio mainly consisting of investment-grade fixed-income securities. The company’s operating performance over the past five years has been consistently positive, with fluctuations driven by rate increases and decreases implemented by the New York Department of Financial Services. Finally, the ratings reflect an upgrade to the company’s ERM assessment to very strong from appropriate. SSL has completed its integration into the Reliance Standard Life operation, including a full integration into the Tokio Marine ERM framework. The Tokio Marine ERM framework has an outstanding track record and affords the company various tools and support mechanisms from the ultimate parent and its subsidiaries.

Partially offsetting these positive rating factors is SSL’s somewhat constrained business profile given its product and geographic concentration, as well as the impact of rate movements on its operations.

The following Long-Term IRs has been affirmed with stable outlooks:

Delphi Financial Group, Inc.—

- “a-” (Excellent) on $175 million fixed/floating rate junior subordinated debentures, due 2037

Reliance Standard Life Global Funding II— “aa+” (Superior) program rating

- “aa+” (Superior) on all outstanding notes issued under the program

For all rating information relating to the release and pertinent disclosures, including details of the office responsible for issuing each of the individual ratings referenced in this release, please see AM Best’s Recent Rating Activity web page. data.title: Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited Announces Filing Of Supplement To MKAR Proxy Statement
data.description:
CALGARY, AB, LONDON, UK, AND VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM:MKA)(TSX-V:MKA) ("Mkango" or the "Company") announces that Mkango Rare Earths Limited ("MKAR") and Crown PropTech Acquisitions ("CPTK") have filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") a supplement (the "Supplement") to the proxy statement/prospectus (the "Proxy Statement/Prospectus") forming part of MKAR's registration statement on Form F-4 (the "Form F-4") relating to the proposed business combination between MKAR and CPTK (the "Proposed Business Combination").

The Supplement, which notes a change in MKAR's proposed board of directors, will be mailed to CPTK shareholders in advance of CPTK's shareholder meeting on 25 November 2026. The Supplement is available on EDGAR at the following hyperlink: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2052373/000121390026122438/ea0313066-424b3_mkango.htm, and will be filed under Mkango's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

About Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited

Mkango is listed on the AIM and the TSX-V Stock Exchanges. Mkango's corporate strategy is to become a market leader in the production of recycled rare earth magnets, alloys and oxides, through its interest in Maginito Limited ("Maginito"), which is owned 79.4 percent by Mkango and 20.6 per cent by CoTec Holdings Corp. ("CoTec"), and the Remloy business acquired by its wholly owned German subsidiary, to develop new sustainable sources of neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium to supply accelerating demand from electric vehicles, wind turbines and other clean energy technologies.

Maginito holds a 100 percent interest in HyProMag Limited and a 90 percent indirect interest in HyProMag GmbH, focused on short loop rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing in the UK and Germany, respectively, and a 100 per cent interest in Mkango Rare Earths UK Limited ("Mkango UK"), focused on long loop rare earth magnet recycling in the UK via a chemical processing route.

Maginito and CoTec are also expanding Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS") recycling technology into the United States via the 50/50 owned HyProMag USA joint venture company.

Remloy has developed a plant in Bitterfeld, Germany, which recycles end-of-life rare earth magnets via a melting process (medium loop rare earth magnet recycling) to produce neodymium-iron-boron ("NdFeB") alloy powders for the bonded and hot deformed magnet markets, complementary to HyProMag's short loop recycling process, to produce sintered magnets, and to Mkango UK's long loop recycling process, to produce mixed rare earth carbonates and oxides.

Mkango currently owns 100 percent of the advanced stage Songwe Hill rare earths project in Malawi and the proposed Pulawy rare earths separation plant in Poland. On grant of the large-scale mining licence the Government of Malawi may elect to take a free 10 percent interest in the entity holding that licence. Both the Songwe and Pulawy projects have been selected as Strategic Projects under the European Union Critical Raw Materials Act, as has HyProMag GmbH. Songwe has also received Development Funding from the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), the U.S. Government's development finance institution, securing US$4.6 million in reimbursable funding for Front End Engineering and Design. MKAR has signed a Business Combination Agreement with CPTK, pursuant to which MKAR, which will hold the Songwe Hill and Pulawy projects, is expected to become listed on Nasdaq, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of closing conditions.

For more information, please visit www.mkangomagneticmaterials.com

CPTK is a Cayman Islands exempted company incorporated in 2020 as a special purpose acquisition company for the purpose of effecting a merger, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses. For further information, visit www.crownproptech.com.

Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements

This news release contains "forward-looking statements" and "forward-looking information" within the meaning of applicable Canadian securities legislation and other applicable securities laws (together, "forward-looking statements"), including statements concerning the mailing of the Supplement and the CPTK shareholder meeting, and the statements under "About Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited" concerning the Proposed Business Combination and the development of Mkango's projects.

Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by forward-looking statements, and readers should not place undue reliance on them. Factors that could cause such differences include: any delay in mailing the Supplement or adjournment of the CPTK shareholder meeting; failure to complete the Proposed Business Combination on the terms and timetable contemplated, or at all, including failure to obtain required approvals, the level of redemptions by CPTK shareholders and the consequences for Mkango's status on AIM and the TSX Venture Exchange, including under Rule 14 of the AIM Rules for Companies; delays in commissioning HyProMag GmbH's plant; the availability of financing; demand and pricing for rare earths; technical, permitting and regulatory matters; political, fiscal and other risks in Malawi, Poland, Germany, the United Kingdom and the United States; the ability to scale recycling technologies to commercial scale; the availability of scrap supplies; and cost overruns.

The foregoing list is not exhaustive. Readers should also consider the risks described in CPTK's filings with the SEC, Mkango's filings on SEDAR+, and the Proxy Statement/Prospectus. Forward-looking statements are made as of the date of this news release. Except as required by applicable law, Mkango assumes no obligation to update or revise them.

Important Information for Investors and Shareholders

In connection with the Proposed Business Combination, MKAR has filed the Form F-4 with the SEC, which includes the Proxy Statement/Prospectus, being a definitive proxy statement of CPTK and a prospectus of MKAR with respect to the securities to be offered in the Proposed Business Combination. The Form F-4 was declared effective by the SEC on November 4, 2026, and CPTK has mailed the Proxy Statement/Prospectus, and is mailing the Supplement, to its shareholders of record as at October 30, 2026. CPTK urges investors and other interested persons to read the Proxy Statement/Prospectus as supplemented, as well as other documents filed with the SEC, because these documents contain important information about the Proposed Business Combination. Such persons can also read CPTK's filings with the SEC for a description of the security holdings of its officers and directors and their respective interests as security holders in the consummation of the transactions described herein. data.title: Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative, The Company Lab, and Outset Ventures Join Forces to Accelerate Quantum Commercialization
data.description:
Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative, The Company Lab, and Outset Ventures Join Forces to Accelerate Quantum Commercialization

The partnership combines Tennessee's quantum ecosystem, commercialization expertise and international venture capital to bring quantum innovation to market faster

The Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative (CQC), The Company Lab (CO.LAB), and New Zealand-based Outset Ventures are combining their strengths to accelerate quantum commercialization, moving quantum innovation from the lab into the hands of the people and industries that can use it.

A memorandum of understanding between the three organizations establishes an international partnership to streamline commercialization, open paths to enterprise customers, and mobilize investment capital. Each organization fulfills a distinct role in the commercialization pathway: CQC leads regional quantum ecosystem development, driving alignment across Tennessee’s research institutions, public-sector assets, and broader economic initiatives. CO.LAB serves as the startup commercialization engine through CO.LAB Q, connecting founders directly with targeted programming, quantum infrastructure providers, corporate pilot opportunities, and enterprise customers across key regional industries. Outset Ventures brings extensive experience backing frontier science, pairing venture capital investment with active deep tech operational support.

“Chattanooga provides the physical infrastructure and testbed capabilities that quantum innovators need to prove their concepts,” said Charlie Brock, CEO of the Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative. “This partnership connects those technical assets directly with commercial opportunities and expanded investment—including joint investment pathways. Tying market access to institutional capital accelerates how quickly these innovations transform from technical promise into market-ready ventures.”

Opportunities enter the partnership through any of the three organizations, triggering a tailored mix of support designed around each startup’s specific needs—ranging from technical validation on real-world testbeds to customer introductions, pilot deployment, and co-investment capital.

“Quantum founders face a unique set of challenges that require specialized infrastructure, real enterprise customers, and investors who truly understand deep tech,” said Tasia Malakasis, CEO of The Company Lab. “Through CO.LAB Q—our dedicated quantum studio—and our partners at Outset and CQC, we can now provide them with direct access to all of those critical enablers.”

The partnership names Chattanooga and Tennessee as a key U.S. market entry hub for ventures across the partners’ international networks. For global founders, the agreement provides a direct landing pad to test technologies on commercial quantum infrastructure and access North American enterprise customers. For Tennessee companies, it creates direct pathways to international capital markets and foreign expansion.

Outset Ventures brings a proven track record of scaling frontier science. Headquartered in Auckland, New Zealand, Outset provides deep tech startups with venture funding, incubation, and specialized laboratory infrastructure—having served as the early home to breakthrough companies like Rocket Lab, LanzaTech, and Mint Innovation. The firm recently closed a NZ$41.5 million fund dedicated to early-stage science and engineering startups.

“Deep tech companies from small markets have to go global early, and the United States is usually the first stop,” said Mat Rowe, Executive Director and Partner at Outset Ventures. “Chattanooga gives our portfolio founders a place where they can test on real infrastructure, connect with enterprise customers, and engage with capital and partners who already understand quantum.”

Isay Acenas, Principal Investor at Outset Ventures and a key driver behind this international partnership, said, “The science is moving quickly. The harder question is how quickly it becomes a product someone buys. This partnership is built around that question, with each of us contributing a critical piece of the pathway.”

Chattanooga is home to the EPB Quantum Center, the nation’s first commercial hub offering quantum networking and quantum computing under one roof. The city is also home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga’s Quantum Center, where more than 25 researchers work across quantum networking, sensing, algorithms and control, and to the Institute for Quantum Innovation, a new research and graduate education center from Vanderbilt University and EPB.

Nearby, Oak Ridge National Laboratory hosts the Department of Energy’s Quantum Science Center, and the state’s $43 million Tennessee Quantum Initiative is investing in quantum infrastructure across Tennessee.

Parties interested in working with the partnership can contact info@chattanoogaquantum.com.

About the Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative

The Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative (CQC) is a nonprofit organization working to establish the Chattanooga and Tennessee region as a nationally recognized, thriving quantum cluster that drives long-term regional economic prosperity. CQC mobilizes regional partners to grow the quantum ecosystem, prepare talent at every level, and help local industry explore and adopt quantum technologies. Learn more at www.ChattanoogaQuantum.com.

About The Company Lab (CO.LAB)

The Company Lab (CO.LAB) is a place-based entrepreneurial support organization accelerating startups in Chattanooga’s industries of strength: energy, mobility, and quantum. By connecting founders with the region’s world-class infrastructure, real-world testbeds, industry expertise, capital, and corporate partners, CO.LAB helps startups validate and scale emerging technologies while advancing corporate innovation priorities. Through this work, CO.LAB strengthens the regional economy and positions Chattanooga as a national hub for commercializing the technologies shaping our future. Learn more at www.thecompanylab.org.

About Outset Ventures

Outset Ventures is a deep technology incubator and early-stage investor based in Parnell, Auckland. Its campus, Future House, is a multistorey research and development facility that is home to more than 20 deep tech companies, a mix of Outset portfolio companies and independent residents. Facility alumni include Rocket Lab, LanzaTech and Mint Innovation, and founders of those companies sit on Outset’s investment committee. Learn more at outset.ventures.
